opencode serve \

  --port 4096 \
  --mdns \
  --mdns-domain mywsldev.local

Bump — this issue has been open for 10 days without any maintainer response.

To add urgency: the unbounded `cache.read` accumulation is not just a cosmetic counting bug. It directly causes **massive token over-consumption** in real usage. Sessions that should have only consumed a few hundred thousand tokens are being accounted as tens of millions, which triggers premature context overflow, failed compaction, and forces expensive re-sends of entire conversation histories.

For anyone hitting the same problem: every long session is silently burning tokens at an inflated rate. This is a **cost and usability regression** that affects all OpenCode users with non-trivial session lengths.

Could a maintainer take a look? The core fix seems straightforward — separate billing/usage totals from effective-context accounting, or exclude `cache.read` from context-window/compaction decisions. Happy to help test or provide more data if needed.

Following up on my own comment — I queried my actual DB and traced the code more carefully. My first take (assistant streaming) was wrong on both the role and the mechanism; here's what's actually going on.

Breaking my ~16GB `event` table down:

| event | rows | total |
|---|---|---|
| `message.updated.1` (role=**user**) | 700 | **16,091 MB** |
| `message.part.updated.1` | 4,679 | 16 MB |
| `message.updated.1` (role=assistant) | 1,773 | 1 MB |

~100% of each big user row is `info.summary.diffs`. The single biggest row was **180 MB** holding **16,609 diff entries (all distinct files)**, each with a full-file patch.

Mechanism:

- `SessionSummary.summarize` (`packages/opencode/src/session/summary.ts`) sets `target.info.summary = { ...summary, diffs }` on the **user** message and calls `sessions.updateMessage(target.info)`. It's triggered both at turn start (`prompt.ts:1304`, `if (step === 1)`) **and on every step-finish** (`processor.ts:745`, forked) — so a multi-step agentic turn re-runs it repeatedly.
- `computeDiff` → `snapshot.diffFull(from, to)` does `git diff --numstat from to -- .` (gitignored files are filtered out), then builds the patch for each remaining file via `structuredPatch(..., { context: Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER })` from the `diff` lib — i.e. the **entire file body** per patch. There's no cap on patch size or entry count (the only size guard, a 2 MB `limit`, applies to untracked-file snapshotting, not the emitted patches). Snapshots are worktree-global (#11802), so a span that touches generated/build trees that aren't gitignored yields thousands of full-file patches → the 180 MB.
- `MessageUpdated` is a `sync`/durable event (`packages/core/src/v1/session.ts`: `sync: { aggregate: "sessionID", version: 1 }`), so `commitSyncEvent` (`packages/core/src/event.ts`) inserts the full encoded `info` — diffs inline — into `event.data`. It's **append-only** (new `seq`/row per publish, no `onConflictDoUpdate` on `EventTable`). The `MessageTable` projection is upserted to a single row, but the event log isn't — so each re-summarize appends another fat row. Hundreds of those = the 16GB.

Net: a worktree-wide, full-file diff is re-serialized into the durable event log every time the user message is summarized. The read tables already hold the latest copy, so the diffs arguably don't need to be in the append-only event at all.

Two fix directions (happy to PR either, with before/after numbers):

1. **Bound `computeDiff` at the source** — also exclude common generated/vendor paths (not just gitignored) and cap per-file/total patch bytes, storing `{file,status,additions,deletions}` with `patch` omitted past the cap (`FileDiff.patch` is already optional and consumers tolerate it). Fixes every downstream copy at once. (#30165 asked for a cap/filter here and was closed not-planned — would a bounded version be acceptable?)
2. **Keep diffs out of the durable encode** — still deliver `summary` on the live notify path (the app sync reducer reads `info.summary.diffs` and the TUI consumes the whole `info`, so it can't just be dropped), but exclude it from the stored `EventTable` payload, since reads/replay come from the message tables. Structural backstop regardless of diff size. (Related: #16741, store per-message diffs separately + lazy-load.)

Could a maintainer confirm which direction fits — bound-at-source, exclude-from-durable-encode, or both?

> As a Simplified Chinese user on Windows, I'd like to add our pain point.
>
> On Windows, the system code page defaults to 936 (GBK), but most modern development tools expect UTF-8 (65001). The typical fix is adding `chcp 65001` to the PowerShell profile. However, since the agent `bash` tool doesn't load the PowerShell profile, Chinese characters in command output become garbled. This significantly hurts the experience for Chinese-speaking developers.
>
> Note that enabling the "Beta: Use Unicode UTF-8 for worldwide language support" option in Windows region settings is **not a viable workaround** for Chinese users — it breaks text rendering in many legacy applications, causing garbled characters in non-Unicode programs. This is a well-known compatibility issue reported by many Chinese users.
>
> A unified shell init behavior (or at least making the `!` shell and agent `bash` tool consistent) would resolve this and make OpenCode much more accessible to the Chinese developer community.
